title: Specializing the Addition Formulas at B = 2*pi to Verify Periodicity
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: What results do you obtain when you substitute B = 2\pi into the cosine and sine addition formulas? Explain how these results agree with a known property of trigonometric functions.

steps.title: Substitute B = 2*pi into the Cosine Addition Formula
steps.explanation: Set B = 2*pi in cos(A + B) = cos A cos B - sin A sin B and substitute cos(2*pi) = 1 and sin(2*pi) = 0.
steps.why: A full rotation of 2*pi radians returns to (1, 0) on the unit circle.

steps.title: Substitute B = 2*pi into the Sine Addition Formula
steps.explanation: Set B = 2*pi in sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B and simplify using cos(2*pi) = 1 and sin(2*pi) = 0.
steps.why: Multiplying by 1 and adding 0 leaves sin A unchanged.

steps.title: Connect to 2*pi-Periodicity
steps.explanation: Both identities confirm that adding a full revolution of 2*pi radians leaves sine and cosine unchanged, agreeing with their 2*pi periodicity.
steps.why: Coterminal angles differing by an integer multiple of 2*pi share identical unit circle coordinates.
